nodes.summary: The Kourovka 20.101 statement that every maximal subgroup of finite index of a finitely generated branch group is normal is false: some finitely generated branch group has a maximal subgroup of finite index that is not normal.
nodes.title: A finitely generated branch group with a non-normal maximal subgroup of finite index

nodes.summary: Kourovka 20.101: finite-index maximal subgroups of finitely generated branch groups are normal. The statement (A. Thillaisundaram) that in every finitely generated branch group every maximal subgroup of finite index is normal.
nodes.title: Kourovka 20.101: finite-index maximal subgroups of finitely generated branch groups are normal

nodes.summary: The Kourovka 15.15 statement that every maximal subgroup of a finitely generated branch group has finite index is false: some finitely generated branch group has a maximal subgroup of infinite index.
nodes.title: A finitely generated branch group with a maximal subgroup of infinite index

nodes.summary: The statement (L. Bartholdi, R. I. Grigorchuk, Z. Šunić) that every maximal subgroup of every finitely generated branch group has finite index.
nodes.title: Kourovka 15.15: maximal subgroups of finitely generated branch groups have finite index

nodes.summary: A faithful level-transitive action of a group $G$ on a rooted tree $T$ is a branch action when, for every level $n$, the rigid stabilizer of level $n$ has finite index in $G$.
nodes.title: Branch action

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a branch group when there exist a rooted tree $T$ (locally finite, with every vertex having at least two children) and a faithful level-transitive action of $G$ on $T$ by tree automorphisms that is a branch action.
nodes.title: Branch group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a branch group if there are a sequence $m \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $m(i) \ge 2$ for all $i$ and an injective homomorphism $\rho$ from $G$ to the permutations of the vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree with branching sequence $m$ such that each $\rho(g)$ is a tree automorphism (for all vertices $v$ and $w$, $v$ is a prefix of $w$ if and only if $\rho(g)(v)$ is a prefix of…
nodes.title: Branch group (Kourovka 15.15)

nodes.summary: For vertices $v$ at level $n$ and $w$ at level $m$ of a rooted tree $T$, $w$ is a descendant of $v$ when $w$ is reached from $v$ by moving from a vertex to one of its children zero or more times: $v$ is a descendant of itself, and a vertex at level $k + 1$ is a descendant of $v$ whenever its parent is.
nodes.title: Descendants in a rooted tree

nodes.summary: Given a faithful level-transitive action of a group $G$ on a rooted tree $T$ and a vertex $v$ of $T$, an element $g \in G$ lies in the rigid stabilizer of $v$ when $g$ fixes every vertex of $T$ that is not a descendant of $v$.
nodes.title: Rigid vertex stabilizer

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a rooted tree with vertex sets $V_n$ at the levels $n \ge 0$ and parent maps $V_{n+1} \to V_n$, and let $G$ be a group. A faithful level-transitive action of $G$ on $T$ consists of an action of $G$ on each level $V_n$ by permutations, that is, a homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{Sym}(V_n)$ for every $n$, such that the actions commute with the parent maps (so $G$ acts by tree automorphisms), only the identity…
nodes.title: Faithful level-transitive action on a rooted tree

nodes.summary: Given a faithful level-transitive action of a group $G$ on a rooted tree $T$ and a level $n$, the rigid stabilizer of level $n$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by the rigid stabilizers of all vertices of $T$ at level $n$.
nodes.title: Rigid stabilizer of a level

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a homomorphism from a group $G$ to the permutations of the vertices of the tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $n$ be a natural number. The $n$-th rigid level stabilizer is the subgroup of $G$ generated by the rigid vertex stabilizers of all vertices at level $n$.
nodes.title: Rigid level stabilizer (Kourovka 15.15)

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a homomorphism from a group $G$ to the permutations of the vertices of the tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $v$ be a vertex. The rigid vertex stabilizer of $v$ is the set of $g \in G$ such that $\rho(g)$ fixes every vertex $w$ of which $v$ is not a prefix, that is, every vertex outside the subtree rooted at $v$.
nodes.title: Rigid vertex stabilizer (Kourovka 15.15)

nodes.summary: A locally finite rooted tree is given by finite sets $V_n$ for $n \ge 0$, the vertices at level $n$, where $V_0$ consists of the root alone, together with parent maps $V_{n+1} \to V_n$, such that every vertex has at least two children: for every $v \in V_n$ there are distinct $x, y \in V_{n+1}$ whose parent is $v$.
nodes.title: Rooted tree given by levels

nodes.summary: For a branching sequence $m \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree are the finite words $(x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ of natural numbers with $x_i < m(i)$ for every $i < k$. The length $k$ of a word is its level and its prefixes are its ancestors.
nodes.title: Vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree (Kourovka 15.15)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
